### THE REGEX AUDIT - MEASURED AGAINST SYNTHETIC LINES, NOT REASONED ABOUT
- **The census first: I ship exactly ONE regex that walks GDScript.**
  - `tools/_l14_test.gd:30` - `(?m)^        ((?:"[a-z]+", )*"[a-z]+"):` - harvests the command verbs
    out of chatcmd.gd's `match` blocks by reading the source as text.
  - `tools/_twitch_parse.gd` - **no pattern-matching of any kind**, and it walks no source. It drives
    the parser through real packets and asserts on the replies.
  - `tools/_commands_doc.gd` - walks **no GDScript**. It loads `data/commands.json` as JSON and
    formats table rows. Its only `replace()` is `|` -> `/` so an arg string cannot break the table.
- **VERDICT ON THE ONE: it PATTERN-MATCHES, it does not parse.** But the specific fault the lead
  pointed at - the one-line form - **IS SAFE HERE, and I proved it rather than assuming either way.**
  The pattern carries **no end anchor**, so `        "delve":    out = _delve(user_id)` matches and is
  read correctly. That is the precise difference from the ad-hoc python regex I faulted on at B155,
  which required the `match` label to END its line and so read 14 reachable commands as unreachable.
  **36 of the 39 label-lines it matches in chatcmd.gd today carry their body on the same line, and all
  36 are harvested correctly.** The shipped instrument never had the bug my scratch instrument had.
- **WHAT IT WOULD MIS-READ.** Each probed against a synthetic line, result recorded:
  - *Silent under-count (INVISIBLE, no failure, just less coverage):* a **tab** indent; **any depth but
    exactly 8 spaces**; `"a","b":` with no space after the comma; `"a",  "b":` with two spaces; any verb
    carrying an **underscore or a digit** (`buy_brew`, `test2`), because the class is `[a-z]+`.
  - *False positive (a FAIL on correct code - the dangerous direction):* **a dictionary literal at the
    same 8-space depth with a lowercase string key.** `        "gold": 140,` reads as a command verb
    named `gold`, and the `missing` arm then demands an entry in `data/commands.json` for a key that is
    not a command. **None exists in chatcmd.gd today** - all 39 matched label-lines are real `match`
    labels - but nothing in the gate prevents one appearing, and the next lane to add an 8-space dict
    to that file turns this gate red for a reason that has nothing to do with the change.
  - *Structural looseness worth naming:* the 39 lines come from **three different `match` blocks** -
    the dispatcher at 150-204, the local-only test block at 313-318, and the help/category block at
    3353-3359 - and the instrument **has no idea which function it is reading.** It merges them. That
    is harmless today because all three dispatch the same vocabulary.
- **WHY THE GATE IS STILL SOUND DESPITE ALL OF THAT, and this is the part that matters:** its second
  arm runs **the other direction** - every key in `data/commands.json` must appear among the harvested
  verbs. A missed label cannot fool that arm, only a false one can. **The published command surface is
  protected structurally, not by the regex's precision.** I am not recommending a change to
  `tools/_l14_test.gd`: it is not my file, the gate is green, and the exposure is a latent false
  positive, not a live hole. I am writing it down so the lane that trips it knows why.

### DRIFT, RE-MEASURED BOTH WAYS ON `c8b46527` - BY BLOCK INDENTATION, NOT BY AN ANCHORED REGEX
- 32 data commands, 31 aliases, **75 code label words at all depths**.
- **PUBLISHED COMMANDS WITH NO CODE LABEL = ZERO.**
- 19 code labels have no entry, and **all nineteen are correct**:
  - **16 are nested argument sub-dispatch**, every one at a depth GREATER than the 8-space dispatcher:
    `title`/`weapon`/`accessories`/`brews` at 12, `treasury`/`score` at 16, `seventy` at 17,
    `kills`/`standing` at 18, `guild`/`mage_tower` at 21, `buy_brew` at 23, `seventh` at 27, and
    `six`/`seven`/`eleven`/`thirteen`/`seventeen` deeper still. Arguments and number words, not
    viewer-callable commands.
  - **3 are `testbits`/`testsub`/`testpoints`**, gated on `local_` at `chatcmd.gd:204` and reachable
    only from Mr. E's own chat box. Publishing them would advertise commands no viewer can run.
  - **The trade, stated plainly:** widening the sweep to all depths buys completeness on the published
    side and costs precision on the code side. That is why these 19 are one note and not nineteen
    findings - which is the same lesson as B155's two corrections, taken forward instead of relearned.
- **NO FILE OF MINE CHANGED.** `scripts/chatcmd.gd`, `data/commands.json` and `docs/COMMANDS.md` are
  byte-identical; `PROGRESS.md` B156 is the only edit in this cycle.
- **Suggestion Box item stays DROPPED**, as the lead's row orders and B154 proved off the published

FOR WHOEVER OWNS tools/_l14_test.gd - THE PATCH, VERBATIM AS PROVED. Replaces the `var rx :=
RegEx.new()` / `rx.compile("(?m)^        ...")` / `search_all` block at tools/_l14_test.gd:29-35.
Call site becomes `var verbs: Array = _harvest(src)`; the `missing` and `unanswered` arms below it
are unchanged. The three helpers and the harvester:

```gdscript
func _strip_comment(line: String) -> String:
	var i := 0
	var n := line.length()
	while i < n:
		var c := line[i]
		if c == "\"":
			i += 1
			while i < n:
				if line[i] == "\\":
					i += 2
					continue
				if line[i] == "\"":
					i += 1
					break
				i += 1
			continue
		if c == "#":
			return line.substr(0, i)
		i += 1
	return line

func _strip_strings(line: String) -> String:
	var out := ""
	var i := 0
	var n := line.length()
	while i < n:
		var c := line[i]
		if c == "\"":
			i += 1
			while i < n:
				if line[i] == "\\":
					i += 2
					continue
				if line[i] == "\"":
					i += 1
					break
				i += 1
			out += "S"
			continue
		if c == "#":
			break
		out += c
		i += 1
	return out

func _indent_of(line: String) -> int:
	var col := 0
	for ch in line:
		if ch == " ":
			col += 1
		elif ch == "\t":
			col += 4 - (col % 4)
		else:
			break
	return col

## The replacement harvester. No depth constant, no end anchor, no 8-space assumption.
func _harvest(src: String) -> Array:
	var verbs: Array = []
	var depth := 0
	var st_ind: Array = []
	var st_lab: Array = []
	var rx_match := RegEx.new()
	rx_match.compile("^match\\b.*:$")
	var rx_lab := RegEx.new()
	rx_lab.compile("^((?:\"[^\"]*\"\\s*,\\s*)*\"[^\"]*\")\\s*:")
	var rx_word := RegEx.new()
	rx_word.compile("^\"([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)\"$")
	for raw in src.split("\n"):
		if raw.strip_edges() == "":
			continue
		var code := _strip_strings(raw)
		if code.strip_edges() == "":
			continue
		var start_depth := depth
		var ind := _indent_of(raw)
		if start_depth == 0:
			while st_ind.size() > 0 and ind <= int(st_ind[st_ind.size() - 1]):
				st_ind.pop_back()
				st_lab.pop_back()
		var body := code.strip_edges()
		var text := _strip_comment(raw).strip_edges()
		if start_depth == 0 and rx_match.search(body) != null:
			st_ind.append(ind)
			st_lab.append(-1)
		elif start_depth == 0 and st_ind.size() > 0:
			var top_ind := int(st_ind[st_ind.size() - 1])
			# only the OUTERMOST match dispatches viewer verbs; a nested `match arg:`
			# inside a label body is argument sub-dispatch, not a command.
			if ind > top_ind and st_ind.size() == 1:
				if int(st_lab[st_lab.size() - 1]) == -1:
					st_lab[st_lab.size() - 1] = ind
				if ind == int(st_lab[st_lab.size() - 1]):
					var m := rx_lab.search(text)
					if m != null:
						var parts := m.get_string(1).split(",")
						var words: Array = []
						var good := true
						for p in parts:
							var mm := rx_word.search(p.strip_edges())
							if mm != null:
								words.append(mm.get_string(1))
							else:
								good = false
						if good:
							for w in words:
								verbs.append(w)
		for ch in code:
			if ch == "(" or ch == "[" or ch == "{":
				depth += 1
			elif ch == ")" or ch == "]" or ch == "}":
				depth -= 1
				if depth < 0:
					depth = 0
	return verbs
```

```gdscript
extends SceneTree
# B160: the B159 replacement harvester for tools/_l14_test.gd:29-35, with the EIGHT
## shape cases and the THREE red-prove arms beside it, so the landing is one paste
## for whoever gets the ownership ruling. Prints B159_HARVEST OK.
## Written at the worktree root and DELETED at the end of the run (the _b2_ask.gd
## precedent). Nothing of this lane is left in the worktree.
var _fail := 0
var _checks := 0

func _ok(c: bool, what: String) -> void:
	_checks += 1
	print(("  ok  " if c else "  FAIL ") + what)
	if not c:
		_fail += 1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- THE PATCH
# Replaces the `var rx := RegEx.new()` / `rx.compile("(?m)^        ...")` /
# `search_all` block at tools/_l14_test.gd:29-35. Call site becomes
#   var verbs: Array = _harvest(src)
# The `missing` and `unanswered` arms below it are unchanged.

func _strip_comment(line: String) -> String:
	var i := 0
	var n := line.length()
	while i < n:
		var c := line[i]
		if c == "\"":
			i += 1
			while i < n:
				if line[i] == "\\":
					i += 2
					continue
				if line[i] == "\"":
					i += 1
					break
				i += 1
			continue
		if c == "#":
			return line.substr(0, i)
		i += 1
	return line

func _strip_strings(line: String) -> String:
	var out := ""
	var i := 0
	var n := line.length()
	while i < n:
		var c := line[i]
		if c == "\"":
			i += 1
			while i < n:
				if line[i] == "\\":
					i += 2
					continue
				if line[i] == "\"":
					i += 1
					break
				i += 1
			out += "S"
			continue
		if c == "#":
			break
		out += c
		i += 1
	return out

func _indent_of(line: String) -> int:
	var col := 0
	for ch in line:
		if ch == " ":
			col += 1
		elif ch == "\t":
			col += 4 - (col % 4)
		else:
			break
	return col

## The replacement harvester. No depth constant, no end anchor, no 8-space assumption.
func _harvest(src: String) -> Array:
	var verbs: Array = []
	var depth := 0
	var st_ind: Array = []
	var st_lab: Array = []
	var rx_match := RegEx.new()
	rx_match.compile("^match\\b.*:$")
	var rx_lab := RegEx.new()
	rx_lab.compile("^((?:\"[^\"]*\"\\s*,\\s*)*\"[^\"]*\")\\s*:")
	var rx_word := RegEx.new()
	rx_word.compile("^\"([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)\"$")
	for raw in src.split("\n"):
		if raw.strip_edges() == "":
			continue
		var code := _strip_strings(raw)
		if code.strip_edges() == "":
			continue
		var start_depth := depth
		var ind := _indent_of(raw)
		if start_depth == 0:
			while st_ind.size() > 0 and ind <= int(st_ind[st_ind.size() - 1]):
				st_ind.pop_back()
				st_lab.pop_back()
		var body := code.strip_edges()
		var text := _strip_comment(raw).strip_edges()
		if start_depth == 0 and rx_match.search(body) != null:
			st_ind.append(ind)
			st_lab.append(-1)
		elif start_depth == 0 and st_ind.size() > 0:
			var top_ind := int(st_ind[st_ind.size() - 1])
			# only the OUTERMOST match dispatches viewer verbs; a nested `match arg:`
			# inside a label body is argument sub-dispatch, not a command.
			if ind > top_ind and st_ind.size() == 1:
				if int(st_lab[st_lab.size() - 1]) == -1:
					st_lab[st_lab.size() - 1] = ind
				if ind == int(st_lab[st_lab.size() - 1]):
					var m := rx_lab.search(text)
					if m != null:
						var parts := m.get_string(1).split(",")
						var words: Array = []
						var good := true
						for p in parts:
							var mm := rx_word.search(p.strip_edges())
							if mm != null:
								words.append(mm.get_string(1))
							else:
								good = false
						if good:
							for w in words:
								verbs.append(w)
		for ch in code:
			if ch == "(" or ch == "[" or ch == "{":
				depth += 1
			elif ch == ")" or ch == "]" or ch == "}":
				depth -= 1
				if depth < 0:
					depth = 0
	return verbs

## The instrument it replaces, kept ONLY as the contrast arm of red-prove 3.
func _harvest_old(src: String) -> Array:
	var rx := RegEx.new()
	rx.compile("(?m)^        ((?:\"[a-z]+\", )*\"[a-z]+\"):")
	var verbs: Array = []
	for mt in rx.search_all(src):
		for w in mt.get_string(1).split(", "):
			verbs.append(w.replace("\"", ""))
	return verbs

# ------------------------------------------------- THE EIGHT SHAPE CASES
# Each case is the source as the harvester sees it and the verbs it must read.
# Cases 1-5 are INVISIBLE to the old 8-space pattern; 6 is its FALSE POSITIVE.
func _cases() -> Array:
	return [
		["1 tab indent",
			"func h(c):\n\tmatch c:\n\t\t\"delve\", \"fish\":\n\t\t\tpass\n",
			["delve", "fish"]],
		["2 label depth 12, not 8",
			"func h(c):\n    match c:\n            \"delve\", \"fish\":\n                pass\n",
			["delve", "fish"]],
		["3 no space after the comma",
			"func h(c):\n    match c:\n        \"inv\",\"bag\":\n            pass\n",
			["inv", "bag"]],
		["4 two spaces after the comma",
			"func h(c):\n    match c:\n        \"inv\",  \"bag\":\n            pass\n",
			["inv", "bag"]],
		["5 underscore and digit in the verb",
			"func h(c):\n    match c:\n        \"buy_brew\":\n            pass\n        \"test2\":\n            pass\n",
			["buy_brew", "test2"]],
		["6 dict key AT label depth - the old false positive",
			"func h(c):\n    match c:\n        \"delve\":\n            var d = {\n        \"gold\": 1,\n            }\n        \"forge\":\n            pass\n",
			["delve", "forge"]],
		["7 dict literal opened inside a body",
			"func h(c):\n    match c:\n        \"delve\":\n            var d = {\n                \"gold\": 1,\n            }\n        \"forge\":\n            pass\n",
			["delve", "forge"]],
		["8 nested `match arg:` is argument sub-dispatch, not commands",
			"func h(c, arg):\n    match c:\n        \"title\":\n            match arg:\n                \"seventh\", \"eleven\":\n                    pass\n        \"forge\":\n            pass\n",
			["title", "forge"]],
	]

func _initialize() -> void:
	for case in _cases():
		var got: Array = _harvest(String(case[1]))
		_ok(got == case[2], "case %s -> %s" % [case[0], got])

	var src := FileAccess.get_file_as_string("res://scripts/chatcmd.gd")
	var verbs: Array = _harvest(src)
	var uniq: Array = []
	for v in verbs:
		if not uniq.has(v):
			uniq.append(v)
	_ok(verbs.size() == 74, "real tree: 74 label words harvested (got %d)" % verbs.size())
	_ok(uniq.size() == 59, "real tree: 59 unique (got %d)" % uniq.size())
	_ok(not verbs.has("gold"), "real tree: `gold` is NOT harvested")
	var cdata: Dictionary = ChatCmd.commands()
	var cs: Dictionary = cdata["commands"]
	var missing: Array = []
	for v in verbs:
		if not cs.has(ChatCmd.canonical(v)) and not v.begins_with("test"):
			missing.append(v)
	var unanswered: Array = []
	for k in cs:
		if not verbs.has(k):
			unanswered.append(k)
	_ok(missing.is_empty() and unanswered.is_empty(), "real tree: drift zero BOTH ways (missing %s / unanswered %s)" % [missing, unanswered])

	var inj := src.replace("        \"memorial\":", "        \"zzznew\":\n            pass\n        \"memorial\":")
	var iv: Array = _harvest(inj)
	var im: Array = []
	for v in iv:
		if not cs.has(ChatCmd.canonical(v)) and not v.begins_with("test"):
			im.append(v)
	_ok(iv.has("zzznew") and im == ["zzznew"], "red 1: an injected `zzznew` label goes RED on missing (%s)" % [im])

	var strp := src.replace("        \"memorial\":", "        \"zzzgone\":")
	var sv: Array = _harvest(strp)
	var su: Array = []
	for k in cs:
		if not sv.has(k):
			su.append(k)
	_ok(not sv.has("memorial") and su.has("memorial"), "red 2: stripping `memorial` loses it AND orphans its data key (%s)" % [su])

	var dictsrc := String(_cases()[5][1])
	var old_g: Array = _harvest_old(dictsrc)
	var new_g: Array = _harvest(dictsrc)
	_ok(old_g.has("gold") and not new_g.has("gold"), "red 3: old harvests gold %s, new does not %s" % [old_g, new_g])

	if _checks < 15:
		_fail += 1
		print("  FAIL only %d checks ran - below the floor of 15" % _checks)
	print(("B159_HARVEST OK (%d checks)" % _checks) if _fail == 0 else ("B159_HARVEST FAIL %d (%d checks)" % [_fail, _checks]))
	quit(0 if _fail == 0 else 1)
```

### (1) THE CORRECTION - `_cut` HAS BEEN PROMISING SOMETHING IT DOES NOT DO
`_cut`'s docstring read *"cut to n characters on a word, never mid-word"*. **That is false, and it
was false when it was written.** The guard is `if sp > int(n / 2)`: it only steps back to a space when
that space sits in the head's **second half**. A head whose last space is at or before n/2 keeps all
n characters and cuts mid-word.

- For `REPLY_MAX` = 440 that needs a 220-character unbroken run. It never fires. Harmless.
- **For `safe_word` it fires every single time.** `safe_word`'s input is one viewer token with no
  space in it at all, so `rfind(" ")` returns -1, -1 is not > 12, and a 25-character word is cut to a
  bare 24 characters mid-word.

**The behaviour is correct and I changed none of it.** There is no word boundary inside a single
token to cut on, and half a nonsense word is the right answer for a 30-character viewer handle. What
was wrong is the comment. I rewrote it to say what the code does, named the `safe_word` case
explicitly, and wrote **NOBODY IS TO "FIX" THE GUARD** into the file - because the next lane to read
"never mid-word" next to a mid-word cut would go hunting a defect that is not there, and that is an
hour the house does not get back.

B173, B174 and B175 spent three firings on the **bare** `!help` line, correctly: it is the widest
thing this lane sends and it grows by `len(name)+2` with every command added. Its **sibling** - the
`!help <command>` detail line built in `help_line()` - had never been measured, and the obvious guess
is that the longest of them sits close behind. **It does not.** Composed off the real

Zero over `REPLY_MAX`. **And it cannot creep up on us the way the bare list does:** this line carries

## B180 - 2026-11-26 11:45 CT firing (chat bot) - THE HELP-LINE ARM WAS WATCHING A CLIFF THAT COULD NEVER BE REACHED, AND THE CUT THAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS IS IN MY OWN FILE, THIRTEEN CHARACTERS LOWER

**A NOTE ON THE LABEL, SO THE LEDGER IS NOT READ WRONG:** B179 titled itself the *11:45* firing but
its lock claim was **11:09:43** and its release **11:11:57**. My own session read the machine clock at
**11:46:29** and claimed at **11:53:42**, so this is the 11:45 slot and B179 was the one before it.
I am not renumbering B179 - the cycle stands as written; only the hour in its title is off.

### WHAT I FOUND, AND IT IS A DEFECT IN MY OWN B138 ARM
The `COMMANDS_DATA HELP LINE CUT` arm existed to catch one thing: a reply of mine growing long
enough that chat loses its tail with nothing logged anywhere. Its budget was **453** = the game
build's `CHAT_MAX_LEN` (480) minus a worst-case `"@<login> "` prefix (27). **That cut can never
happen.** Every answer leaves through `safe_line()` (chatcmd.gd:293), which caps at
`REPLY_MAX` **440** via `_cut`, and `twitch_reply.emit` is handed that capped line
(chatcmd.gd:303-305). The worst message `twitch_eventsub.gd:1248` can be built from it is
`27 + 440 = 467` - **under its own 480**, so its truncation branch is dead code from this lane's side.

**So the arm sat THIRTEEN CHARACTERS ABOVE the real cliff.** A reply of **441..453** characters was
truncated *in my own file*, silently, while the arm reported nothing over budget - the exact fault it
was written to catch, one cliff too late. And `_cut` is the *worse* of the two cuts to be blind to:
the game build's appends `"..."`, while `_cut` backs up to the last space past `n/2` and strips a
trailing comma or dash, so **the tail goes with no marker at all** and the line still reads as a
finished sentence. What sits at that tail on the longest line this file emits is the hub URL.

### THE FIX, AND WHY IT ALSO REMOVES A DEPENDENCY
`var hl_budget: int = mini(REPLY_MAX, hl_cap - hl_pre)` - the arm now fires on **whichever cut comes
first**. The 480 mirror is kept and labelled the *second* cliff: it is dead while `REPLY_MAX <= 453`,
and if the game build ever lowers `CHAT_MAX_LEN` below 467 `mini()` picks it up without my touching
this file. The old comment's worry - "if the game build moves CHAT_MAX_LEN, this arm's number has to
follow it" - no longer decides when the arm fires. Both fault messages now name which cliff bound the
budget, `REPLY_MAX`, and the prefix-adjusted cap, so the printed line says what it measured against.

### GATE RESULTS - VERDICT LINES, NOT RETURN CODES

  lines are `COMMANDS_DATA MINIBOSS UNNAMED - 1 bodies ... ["overlooker"]` - **the game build's row,
  not mine, an ELEVENTH consecutive firing.** B168's 65 -> 1 ERROR drop holds.
- **RED-PROVE (the arm is not asserted):** padding `forge`.short alone to put its help line at **446**
  characters fired `COMMANDS_DATA HELP LINE CUT - 1 reply(s) over the 440-char first cut (REPLY_MAX
  440, prefix-adjusted cap 453) ... ["!help forge is 446 chars, 6 over"]`. **446 is UNDER the old 453,
  so the arm as it stood this morning would have printed NOTHING.** That is the blind band proved at

## B183 - 26 Nov 2026, 17:45 CT firing. THE `example` IS THE ONE FIELD A VIEWER TYPES VERBATIM AND SEVEN OF EIGHT WERE UNWATCHED - AND THE SAME INJECT PROVED MY OWN LANE'S COMMITTED NOTE FALSE.

**Two claims, seven launches, never two Godots at once, every launch declared in advance.**

### 1. The hole, measured before a line was written
`get("example")` is read in exactly **two** places in `scripts/chatcmd.gd`: the `DYE EXAMPLE GHOST`
arm, and `help_line()` - which **publishes** it, as `e.g. !wear corgi`, on the `!help <command>`
detail line. So of the **eight** examples that carry an argument, **one** was watched:

| example | authority | watched before B183 |
|---|---|---|
| `!dye teal` | items.json dyes | YES (`DYE EXAMPLE GHOST`) |
| `!forge spear` | `Gear.KINDS` | no |
| `!enlist knight dwarf` | `Roster.CLASSES` / `SPECIES` | no |
| `!respec cleric` | `Roster.CLASSES` | no |
| `!brew quickwater 2` | `data/potions.json` | no |
| `!wear corgi` | `Roster.item_key()` | no |
| `!miniboss Ordrik` | `_miniboss_find()` | no |
| `!help forge` | the command table | no |

An example is not a published *word*, it is a published **instruction**. `wear`'s own refusal is
`"No such thing for sale in Bellmire. !help wear lists them."` - it sends the viewer back to the
line that just lied to them, and nothing logs anywhere.

### 2. Three arms, and they resolve rather than pattern-match
`EXAMPLE MISSING` (no `example` at all - `help_line()` falls back to a bare `!<key>`),
`EXAMPLE VERB` (the example's own `!verb` is neither the key nor a published alias - this one
covers all 32), `EXAMPLE GHOST` (the argument resolves to nothing). Every word tested is read out
of `data/commands.json` at load and handed to **the same function the live command uses**, so the
arm cannot drift from the behaviour it guards and it restates no published word.

**All seven resolve today and I measured all seven by hand first**, so this landed green. Two are
thin and the thinness is the point:
- `!wear corgi` resolves **only** through `item_key`'s NAME path. items.json has no `corgi` key -
  it has `pet_corgi` ("a corgi") and `pet_corgi_pup` ("a corgi pup"), and `item_key` trims a
  leading `"a "` off the name. If that name stops being exactly "a corgi", the word falls to the
  substring branch, **both** pet rows contain "corgi", two hits is no hit, and the example dies.
  The live pet pool is being changed by the game build **this day**.
- `!miniboss Ordrik` resolves only because `Ordrik` is an `MB_NAME` **value** on `beadle`, from the
  C-130 rename still pending Mr. E's final say.
